links.outcome: Rate at which surgeons accepted incorrect mock AI incision guidance (automation bias) and ability to detect incorrect outputs
links.effect: Surgeons accepted incorrect AI suggestions in 60.6% of incorrect-overlay frames (43/71); specificity for rejecting incorrect guidance 39.4% (28/71); correct suggestions accepted 76.9%; confidence rose after AI exposure (+0.65, P<.001).
links.quote: Surgeons accepted approximately 3 of every 5 incorrect AI recommendations.

screen.reason: Empirical study measuring automation bias and clinician override failure (assessing clinician-in-the-loop oversight as a safety mechanism) using simulated AI overlays in robotic surgery decision-making.

primary.practice: clinician review and oversight of AI recommendations
